newsitem.title: USA: Gaylord CEO says may pursue other deals.
newsitem.headline: Gaylord CEO says may pursue other deals.

text.p: Gaylord Entertainment Co President and Chief Executive E.W. Wendell Monday said the firm "is not afraid to enter into new ventures or pursue the acquisition of other companies."
The comments were released in a statement, reflecting remarks that Wendell made to company employees.
Earlier, Gaylord and Westinghouse Electric Corp agreed that Westinghouse would acquire, by merger, Gaylord's two major cable networks, TNN (The Nashville Network), and CMT (Country Music Television).

The company saw the further growth of TNN and CMT best served if it was part of a larger firm that "can use its leverage to help take country music to a higher level of visibility" in the U.S., he said.

Wendell said the core of the company's business will still be centered around country music, and noted that the expansion of its hospitality operations to other markets is another growth strategy it will pursue.

Gaylord will seek to make its tourism assets bigger contributors to the bottom line, he said. Those properties include the Grand Ole Opry, the Opryland Theme Park, Ryman Auditorium and the General Jackson Showboat.

Contemporary Christian music is also an entertainment area the company sees as having high growth potential, Wendell said. He also noted that music publishing will continue as a growth vehicle for Gaylord.
